title: Start with one person
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How do you start a talk with a stranger?
Jose said that it is the same process for one person as for a thousand: you run into somebody at a coffee shop and start a conversation.
A student suggested using visual clues. Jose said to be careful, because a wealthy person may be dressed in rags.
A student said: start with vague, broad questions and then more specific ones based on how they answer.
Jose said that is a needs assessment: asking questions to discover what the other person is interested in, whether in a coffee shop or on a sales call.
Another gave an icebreaker: I have never been in this shop; what do you get? Whatever they say is the right answer.
Jose said: lower the pressure of calling, and do not be clichéd. You want an energy in those calls, which takes discipline when you make thirty or forty a day.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a question you could ask a stranger.
Write the follow-up that goes deeper.
Write your icebreaker for a call.
Write how you lower the pressure.
Write your call to action for the first call.
